title: Gaps and niches in the market
log: 2026-11-04T17:58:50Z autoreview: cleared with the fix (a wording)

draft.title: Gaps and niches in the market
card: a need that buyers have but nobody is meeting, or nobody is meeting well. A business that spots a gap can fill it and earn sales.
a small group of buyers with special wants, such as left-handed players or people who cannot eat gluten. A niche market is small, but it may be poorly served.
Big businesses often aim at the largest group of buyers. This can leave gaps and niches for small businesses to serve.
Businesses find gaps and niches by listening to customers, noticing complaints and looking at what is missing from the shops nearby.
draft.remember: Look for what buyers want but cannot easily get, or for a small group with special wants.

a.q: Which of these is a niche market?
opts: Vegan dog treats for owners who avoid animal products
Bread sold to households across a whole state
Petrol sold to drivers in a large city
Milk sold in every supermarket in Australia
a.why: A niche is a small group of buyers with special wants, and vegan dog treats suit only a few owners. The other three are sold to large groups of buyers, so they are not niches.
a.clue: Which one is aimed at a small group with special wants?

b.q: Mia lives in a small town in Tasmania. She hears many people say they must drive two hours to get their bikes repaired. She opens a bike repair shop. What has she done?
opts: Filled a gap by meeting a need nobody was meeting
Entered a crowded market full of repair shops
Copied a big business that serves most buyers
Created a need that buyers did not have before
b.why: People already wanted bike repairs but could not get them nearby, so Mia filled a gap. The need was there already, so she did not create it, and no other shops were serving it.
b.clue: Was anyone nearby meeting the need?

a.best: Vegan dog treats for owners who avoid animal products

b.best: Filled a gap by meeting a need nobody was meeting

problems.detail: The right option stands out. It is clearly the longest and the only one with a qualifying detail ('for owners who avoid animal products'). The other three are short, generic mass-market products, so a student could pick it without knowing what a niche is. Make the distractors similar in length and detail, for example other specific but large-market products.

a.q: Which of these is a niche market?
opts: Vegan dog treats for owners who avoid animal products
White bread for families who shop at supermarkets
Regular petrol for drivers who fill up in big cities
Full cream milk for shoppers who buy groceries weekly
a.why: A niche is a small group of buyers with special wants. Owners who want vegan treats for their dogs are a small group with a special want. Bread, petrol and milk buyers are huge groups with ordinary wants, so they are not niches.
a.clue: Which group of buyers is small and wants something unusual?
